text: Here's the strange part. Many naval architects think a head-on hit might have saved her. The bow would have crumpled, flooding perhaps the first two compartments. Well within what the ship could survive. In eighteen seventy-nine, a steamship called the Arizona hit an iceberg head-on. Her bow was crushed, and she still made it to port. But a head-on crash would have been deadly for anyone in the bow, and turning away is every sailor's instinct. Nobody had time to calculate.
